name: KASCADE
notes: The KASCADE array is placed at the existing site:kit-campus-north (a campus-grade point). The sources give the array position only as "49,1°N, 8,4°O" (0.1 degree), which does not distinguish it from the campus point; no separate site is created.
KASCADE sits at facility:kit-karlsruhe, whose only recorded interval starts in 2019 (KATRIN); the validator therefore warns that this experiment predates its facility. For the integrator.
KASCADE-Grande (2003 extension, with LOPES radio antennas) is a separate record: experiment:kascade-grande.

physics_goals.note: The page describes the combined KASCADE and KASCADE-Grande experiments.
physics_goals.quote: KASCADE – Grande was an extensive air shower experiment array to study the cosmic ray primary composition and the hadronic interactions in the energy range E0=1016-1018eV
physics_goals.value: Study the cosmic-ray primary composition and the hadronic interactions around the knee of the energy spectrum.

summary.plain: KASCADE was an array of particle detectors on the Karlsruhe research campus that measured the electrons, muons and hadrons of cosmic-ray air showers. It showed the "knee" of the spectrum comes from light elements running out.
summary.technical: KArlsruhe Shower Core and Array DEtector: 200 m × 200 m array of scintillation detectors (electromagnetic and muon), a muon tracking detector and a hadron calorimeter at 110 m a.s.l.; measured spectra of elemental groups around the knee (3-5 PeV). Ran 1996-2012; extended by KASCADE-Grande in 2003.
